title: Drag a shapes corner to round it
goal: Rounding one corner of a shape means typing a number into the panel. Photoshop and every drawing tool let you grab a small handle just inside a corner and pull it, watching the curve follow your hand. Give a picked shape that handle, one per corner, so rounding is something you do on the canvas rather than something you type.
notes: Follow-up from the audit for each-corner-of-a-shape-can-be-rounded-on-its-own (queue/audits/2026-09-08-each-corner-rounded.json, rough item 2). The model is already there: PhotonzCore/CornerRadii.swift with per corner numbers, and PhotonzDocument.setCornerRadius(layerIDs:corner:to:) writes one corner. What is missing is the canvas handle. Handles live in Sources/Photonz/CanvasDisplay.swift beside the eight resize handles; the outline itself already curves per corner via SelectionOutlineShape.path(box:cornerRadii:). Flag: next-shape-parts.
acceptance: A picked shape with corners shows a small handle just inside each of its four corners
Dragging one handle rounds that corner alone and the shape follows the hand live
Holding a modifier while dragging one handle rounds all four together
Letting go records one undo step, and the panel Corner Radius rows show what was dragged

log.note: Adversarial review before building. (1) The task asks for drag-one-corner by default and a modifier for all four, which is the reverse of Photoshop and Figma, where dragging a corner widget rounds all four and Option isolates one. Building it as asked anyway: the panel slider is already the all-four control, so what the canvas adds is the per corner pull, and Option is the key that switches modes in Photoshop too, just pointed the other way. The question goes into the audit's evaluate list so the user can rule on it rather than me guessing. (2) Cut: four dots inside EVERY selected object would be noise in a redlining app where most selections are a screenshot or a measurement. Handles are offered only on shapes that have corners (rectangle, highlight). Pictures, groups and text still round from the panel. (3) Cut: no readout pill chasing the drag. The shape itself follows the hand and the panel row is already on screen; a floating number is decoration. (4) Collision check: the rest position is 12 screen points in along both axes from a corner, so a radius handle sits about 17 screen points from the corner resize square. Both carry 6 point tolerances, so they never overlap, and the radius hit runs BEFORE the frame handle branch so Option over a radius handle rounds rather than skews. (5) A cramped shape must not wear them: reuse Handles.crampedSpan, so a frame too small to keep its edge midpoints is too small for radius handles too. (6) Rotated and skewed layers read through the same handle space conversion the frame handles use, or the dots would draw in one place and answer in another. (7) A press on a radius handle no longer moves the shape from those four spots. Same trade a collage slot and a measure foot already make: pick it first, then the inner handles appear.

Shipped behind the Next-only flag next-corner-handles, on by default. PhotonzCore/CornerRadiusHandles.swift places the dots (12 screen points in from a square corner, at the arc's CENTRE once rounded, which is the one placement that travels a point for every point the hand does; sitting it on the arc would creep 3 points over a 50 point pull), hit-tests them, turns a pointer into a radius, and answers whether a frame is roomy enough at all (Handles.crampedSpan, the same threshold the edge midpoints use). Layer.offersCornerRadiusHandles limits them to shapes with corners; Layer.rounded(_:) gives the chrome a picture of the drag. 26 core tests, all 5264 tests green. App side: CanvasView holds the CornerRadiusDrag plus a cornerRadiusHandlesLayer, CanvasPointerDrags reads the dots BEFORE the frame handles so Option there means all four corners rather than skew, CanvasDisplay draws them and curves the blue outline by the live number, and CanvasPointerCue gives them the open hand and keeps the copy badge off them. EditorState.cornerRadiiPreview is the fix for something the probe caught: mid-drag the shape was visibly round while the panel still read 0 px, so the corner rows now read the in-flight drag and the two agree. Verified live in the probe with Scripts/playtest/corner-drag-rounds-walk.json, which asserts 50/0/0/0 after a single corner pull, 25 on all four after an Option pull, 50/0/0/0 again after ONE undo, and 0 after pulling the same dot back out past the corner, plus pictures of a 30x30 shape wearing no dots and a rotated shape whose dots turned with it. 17 corner/round/shape walks pass. Full sweep requested: press precedence changed for every picked shape.
